input.question: What is the latest stable version of Python (as of your most recent knowledge), and what was its release date?
input.context: The learner is explicitly testing whether the background web-research tool works. A current-version fact is a good probe: verifiable, and not something I would state from memory with full confidence.

result.brief:
## Summary
As of the most recent python.org release data, the latest stable Python version is Python 3.15.2, released October 25, 2026. The latest feature (minor) release series is Python 3.15, whose first stable version, 3.15.0, was released October 9, 2026.

## Findings
1. **Latest stable release: Python 3.15.2** — python.org's download and source-release pages list "Latest Python 3 Release: Python 3.15.2" as the current stable version, with the official release page giving a release date of Oct. 25, 2026. It is the second maintenance release of the 3.15 series. [Download Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/), [Python Release Python 3.15.2](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3152/)

2. **Feature release baseline: Python 3.15.0 on 9 October 2026** — the "What's new in Python 3.15" documentation states that "Python 3.15 is the latest stable release of the Python programming language" and that "Python 3.15 was released on 9 October 2026." The downloads page confirms 3.15 first released 2026-10-09, with bugfix maintenance status and end of support planned for 2031-10 per PEP 790. [What's new in Python 3.15](https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.15.html), [Python documentation by version](https://www.python.org/doc/versions/)

3. **3.15.2 is a security-driven release** — it is an expedited security release containing roughly 130 bugfixes, build improvements, and documentation changes from 70 contributors since 3.15.1, including CVE-2026-115557 (distrust of compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys in the `ssl` module), CVE-2026-114583 (tarfile link-replacement fix), and a `http.cookiejar` cookie-version fix. [Python Release Python 3.15.2](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3152/)

4. **Other active series for context** — as of the same date, Python 3.14.10 was the latest bugfix release of the 3.14 series (first released 2025-10-07, supported until 2030-10), and Python 3.13 was in security-only status (3.13.18, released Oct. 25, 2026). Python 3.16 is in pre-release with first release planned for 2027-10-06. [Download Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/), [Python Source Releases](https://www.python.org/downloads/source/)

## Sources
- Kept: Python Release Python 3.15.2 (https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3152/) — primary source for the exact latest stable version and its release date
- Kept: Download Python | Python.org (https://www.python.org/downloads/) — official index of active releases and maintenance status
- Kept: What's new in Python 3.15 (https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.15.html) — confirms 3.15 as the latest stable release and the 3.15.0 release date
- Kept: Python documentation by version (https://www.python.org/doc/versions/) — full release history with dates per version
- Dropped: Python 3.13.18 and 3.13.17 release pages — relevant only as superseded/security releases, not the latest stable version
- Dropped: Windows releases page (https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/) — platform-specific duplicate of the same version information

## Gaps
- The question asked for the version "as of your most recent knowledge." The answer reflects live web research current to the python.org release pages, which show releases dated October 2026. If the actual current date differs from that, the python.org downloads page should be re-checked before teaching, since Python maintenance releases (3.15.3, etc.) arrive on a roughly monthly cadence.
- Nothing else was unanswerable; the version number and both release dates were directly confirmed from primary official sources.
